aboutStory.headline: Welcome to the District
aboutStory.body: Curry District is a whole neighborhood of flavor on FM 423 in Little Elm, and the menu is your map. Head down one street for Andhra-style fire: Karampodi Chicken with a serious chili-powder kick and Gongura Mutton Pulav, tangy and bold. Turn the corner for North Indian tandoor classics, glowing hot: Tandoori Chicken, Chicken Tikka Kabab and garlic naan that vanishes faster than you can say ‘bas, ek aur.’ Biryani Boulevard is home to our dum biryani, layered, sealed and steaming. Down Indo-Chinese Alley, Gobi Manchurian and Chilli Paneer bring the wok-tossed street-food swagger. And Butter Chicken? It basically has its own zip code. Bring the family after practice, grab pickup on the way home or let us feed the whole party. Tell us your heat level. We’ll handle the swaad.

aboutStory.headline: A generous table in Little Elm
aboutStory.body: Curry District sets a generous Indian table on FM 423 in Little Elm, and our menu travels far to fill it. There is Andhra-style fire: Karampodi Chicken, deep with chili, and Gongura Mutton Pulav, bright with tangy gongura leaves. There are North Indian tandoor classics: Tandoori Chicken and Chicken Tikka Kabab with charred edges, and garlic naan torn warm at the table. Our dum biryani is layered, sealed and slow-steamed, so the lid lifts on a cloud of fragrance. And for a playful turn, Indo-Chinese street favorites such as Gobi Manchurian and Chilli Paneer arrive glossy from the wok. We cook for the neighborhood: weeknight dinners, birthday tables and the friends you have been meaning to see. Choose your spice level, gather your people and stay a while.

rules: One Hindi phrase per screen, max. Bazaar voice only.
Gloss it in English the first time it appears on a page (inline or as a Caveat-script aside).
Never use Hindi in hours, addresses, prices, allergen or legal text, or as the only label on a button.
Wrap Romanized Hindi in <span lang="hi-Latn"> and Devanagari in <span lang="hi">.
Have a native Hindi speaker (ideally the owners) sign off before print.

devanagari.meaning: ‘Curry District’ written phonetically in Devanagari. It is a transliteration, not a translation.
devanagari.spellingCheck: करी (ka + ra + ii) is the standard Hindi spelling of the loanword 'curry'. डिस्ट्रिक्ट (dda+i, sa+virama, tta+virama, ra+i, ka+virama, tta) is the standard phonetic rendering of 'district'. Code points checked; nukta-free, NFC-normal.
devanagari.usage: Optional decorative accent only (stamp borders, sticker rims, mural lettering, packaging seals). Never replaces the English name; mark it aria-hidden="true" when decorative, or lang="hi" when read aloud.
devanagari.fontNote: The brand font files are Latin-only subsets and cannot render Devanagari. Vendor a Devanagari face (OFL), e.g. Yatra One or Rozha One (display) or Noto Sans Devanagari (text), via npm @fontsource, subset to these glyphs. Without it phones fall back to a system font.
devanagari.status: spelling verified by code point; native-speaker sign-off recommended before print
